Measure L — Library Services Funding Act

What is Measure L?

Plain facts about the library funding measure on the June 18 ballot — what it does, what it costs, and what happens to your library without it.

The short version

Measure L is a special assessment that provides dedicated, stable funding for the Evergreen Public Library's day-to-day operations. It costs the average household approximately $3.20 per month — about $38 per year — based on property value.

Without this funding, the library's director has announced it will be forced to make immediate and severe service cuts beginning July 1, 2026.

If the measure passes vs. fails

✔ If Measure L Passes
  • Open 7 days a week, including all day Sunday
  • Evening hours until 8pm on weekdays
  • Children's programs, story time, and summer reading continue
  • After-school homework help program protected
  • 24 public computers available with free internet
  • Job-search workshops and résumé assistance maintained
  • Building repairs can proceed
  • All 12 full-time staff positions retained
✕ If Measure L Fails
  • 18 hours per week cut from open schedule
  • Closed every Sunday, starting July 1
  • Youth programs reduced by 40%
  • After-school homework help eliminated
  • Computer lab hours cut; possible reduction in machines
  • Job-search support suspended
  • Roof repairs and building maintenance delayed indefinitely
  • Hiring freeze; potential staff reductions

How the funding works

  • 1

    Voters approve Measure L on June 18

    A simple majority is required. Every registered voter in Evergreen can vote on this measure regardless of property ownership.

  • 2

    Assessment applied to property tax bills

    Beginning with the next fiscal year, a special assessment is applied to property tax bills based on assessed property value. The average household pays $3.20/month.

  • 3

    Funds go directly to library operations

    Measure L funds are dedicated exclusively to library operations — they cannot be redirected to other city uses. The library board oversees spending with annual public audits.

  • 4

    Services are maintained and stable

    With dedicated funding, the library can plan ahead, maintain services, and invest in programming — instead of operating year-to-year in uncertainty.
